summary: Spec-kit core mostly enforces what its notes promise, but several gates fail open or give a different answer depending on how they are called. Gate 3 depends on word order, the resume branch can skip it despite its own always-required comment, and a phase parent passes ANCHORS_VALID without any anchor being read. Root resolution is the widest risk: four resolvers disagree, and the continuity writer falls back to the shared runtime checkout when a project is not recognised, writing there after one stderr line. The save writer itself is an untracked build output that the install probe does not check and the printed repair does not build. Exit codes are the most common UX defect: check-goal --all, the trigger lookup and the post-edit placeholder check each return a status that disagrees with the result they print.
recommendations:
1. Make gate-3-classifier.ts treat any write trigger as a write regardless of its position (:731), and make the resume branch honour its always-required contract (:840-842).
2. Have resolveProjectRoot refuse, not fall back, when the project is not recognised (config.ts:142-146), and test usesSpecKit on the authored SKILL.md sentinel under either .skilled or .opencode.
3. Track or build-check runtime/cli/dist: point /doctor:install at runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js and change the repair line in validate.sh to the skill-root build that includes runtime/cli.
4. Parse anchors for phase parents in ANCHORS_VALID instead of returning pass at orchestrator.ts:975.
5. Align exit codes with printed results: check-goal --all (:703), the unfiltered trigger lookup (:204), and the post-edit placeholder wrapper against the Draft deferral in the rule.
6. Keep research and review folders out of the trigger corpus hash so an in-progress packet does not churn it.
open_questions: Should create.sh resolve templates from the runtime checkout rather than the target repo, or is per-repo template override the intended contract?
Is SCOPE_ADHERENCE, named in the v4.0.0.0 note but absent from the validator registry, retired or never built?
